services.title: Free Roof Inspection
services.short: A complete roof assessment at no cost to you.
services.text: A trained inspector evaluates and documents your roof's condition, then explains the findings in plain language. No cost, no obligation.

body: Every Houston homeowner knows the anxiety that follows a severe storm. Was the roof damaged? Will insurance cover the repairs? Our inspectors eliminate the guesswork with a thorough inspection that costs you nothing.
We inspect every inch of the roof system, photograph what we find, and prepare a written findings report you can submit to your insurer.
points: Hail damage assessment: impact marks, granule loss and exposed mat
Wind damage evaluation: lifted, missing or torn shingles
Water intrusion points and active leak sources
Flashing, valleys, penetrations and edge details
Gutter and drainage check
Roof deck and structural integrity
Attic ventilation and moisture control
Complete photographic documentation for insurance claims

faqs.a: Nothing. The inspection is free and there is no obligation afterwards.

faqs.q: What do I get at the end?
faqs.a: A written findings report with photographs of the damage, explained in plain language, that you can send to your insurance company.

services.title: Impact-Resistant Shingles
services.short: Class 3 and Class 4 shingles that may lower your premium.
services.text: Class 3 and Class 4 impact-rated shingles under UL 2218, built for Houston hail and Gulf winds, and often eligible for an insurance discount.
services.imageAlt: Overlapping shingles laid across a roof slope
body: Class 3 shingles withstand a 1.75-inch steel ball dropped from 20 feet under UL 2218. Class 4, the highest rating, withstands a 2-inch steel ball from the same height and uses SBS-modified polymer technology for flexibility in extreme temperatures.
Many Texas insurers offer premium discounts for Class 3 and Class 4 shingles. Check with your insurer for the specific discount available on your policy.
points: Class 3: UL 2218 1.75-inch steel ball test
Class 4: UL 2218 2.0-inch steel ball test, the highest rating
Wind resistance ratings from 110 to 130 MPH
Class 4 lines from CertainTeed, Owens Corning, Atlas, IKO, Tamko and GAF
May qualify for a TWIA wind and hail premium discount
Houston averages 3 to 4 significant hailstorms a year
Class 4 shingles are designed to resist cracking and splitting from large hailstones

services.title: TWIA WPI8 Compliance
services.short: Roofs installed to the windstorm standard your certificate needs.
services.text: We install every roof to TWIA windstorm standards so you can obtain or maintain the WPI8 certificate your wind and hail coverage depends on.
body: A WPI8, the Windstorm Certificate of Compliance, verifies that your roof and structure meet Texas Department of Insurance building code requirements for windstorm resistance. It is required to obtain or maintain windstorm insurance through TWIA in designated coastal areas, which include parts of the Houston-Galveston region.

TWIA serves 14 counties and one part of Harris County along the Texas coast. In a designated catastrophe area, standard homeowner policies typically exclude wind and hail coverage, which makes TWIA the primary option.
points: Roofs installed using TDI-approved methods and materials
A licensed TDI windstorm inspector conducts the on-site inspection
The inspector issues the WPI8 certificate when the roof passes
The certificate is filed with TWIA for your wind and hail coverage
Impact-resistant shingles can qualify you for a TWIA premium discount
Class 4 shingles can save up to 35% on your annual TWIA premium, and more alongside hurricane clips and sealed roof decking
Properties in Galveston, Brazoria, Chambers and parts of Harris County may fall in these zones
Help documenting wind and hail damage for a TWIA claim

faqs.q: Do I need a WPI8 certificate?
faqs.a: If your property sits in a TWIA-designated catastrophe area, you need a valid WPI8 to qualify for wind and hail insurance. Without it you may not be able to get coverage, or your premiums could be significantly higher.
A licensed TDI windstorm inspector, after an on-site inspection of the completed roof. Our part is installing to the standard the inspection checks.

faqs.q: How do I look up my certificate?
faqs.a: Search by property address or certificate number on the official TWIA certificate search portal at twia.org, which shows your current WPI8 windstorm certificate status.

faqs.q: How soon should I file a TWIA claim?
faqs.a: As soon as possible after wind or hail damage, because Texas law requires you to report damage promptly. We help document the damage and work with your adjuster. TWIA makes all coverage decisions independently.

facts.heading: Loss statement review
facts.text: We compare your insurer's Explanation of Loss against our documented damage report, and prepare a supplemental claim with supporting evidence where covered items were missed or undervalued. Supplements are common and may take additional time, and the revised determination is your carrier's.

facts.heading: What we are and are not
facts.text: Houston Roof Claims LLC is a roofing contractor, not an insurance company, a public adjuster or an attorney. We document damage and guide you through the process, and we do not guarantee claim outcomes: coverage and payment amounts are determined solely by your insurance carrier under your policy terms.

items: Check for missing or damaged shingles after every storm

Inspect the attic for water stains or daylight
Document any visible damage with photos

Inspect flashing around chimneys and skylights

Note any new interior water stains
